identity.title: 1.3-mm ALMA observations of the Fomalhaut debris system
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present ALMA Band 6 observations (1.3 mm/233 GHz) of Fomalhaut and its debris disc.

evidence.quote: Observations were centred on Fomalhaut using J2000 coordinates RA = 22 h 57 min 39.44 s and $\delta = -29^{\circ} 37' 22.64''$.
Located at a distance of $7.66 \pm 0.04$ pc (cite: hipparcos)

Observations were centred on Fomalhaut using J2000 coordinates RA = 22 h 57 min 39.44 s and $\delta = -29^{\circ} 37' 22.64''$.
Located at a distance of $7.66 \pm 0.04$ pc (cite: hipparcos)

question.value: What is the 1.3 mm morphology of Fomalhaut's debris ring, its mm spectral index and grain size slope, and is there central emission in excess of the stellar photosphere indicating an inner debris component?

evidence.quote: The observations are thus able to address whether there is indeed excess over the stellar emission, constraining the presence of an inner debris disc or ring.
The data were acquired as part of the ALMA cycle 2 campaign (project ID 2013.1.00486.S).
The observations were taken in band 6 (at $\sim233$ GHz)

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: TDM, dual polarization, 4 spws of 2 GHz at 224, 226, 240, 242 GHz, 128 channels of 15.625 MHz

evidence.quote: Four different spectral windows were used with 2 GHz bandpasses at rest frequency centres of 224, 226, 240, and 242 GHz.
A 34-antenna configuration was used; the longest baseline was 1.1 km.
The size of the synthetic beam is $0.329 \times 0.234$ arcsec at a position angle of 83.6$^{\circ}$.
The observations achieve a sensitivity of 17 $\mu$Jy

time_on_source.value: three EBs, average integration time 1.08 hr

evidence.quote: The average integration time was 1.08 hr.
Observations were made in three execution blocks (EBs) taking place between 2015 June 11$^{\rm th}$ and 2015 September 21$^{\rm st}$.

what.value: Literature disc and stellar flux densities 70 um-6.6 mm and 0.554-24 um used in SED and spectral index fits (Table flux_list)

evidence.quote: with literature values for flux densities at different wavelengths (see Table [\[flux_list\]](#flux_list)).

external_data_from_literature.citation: Ricci 2012, Boley 2012, Su 2016, Holland 2003/1998, Acke 2012, Ishihara 2010, Pickles 2010, Boyajian 2013

evidence.quote: The photosphere temperature of the star is constrained to be T$_{B} = 8600 \pm200$ K from *Herschel* observations (cite: acke).

pipeline_or_manual.value: CASA reduction: WVR, Tsys, bandpass, flux, phase calibration

evidence.quote: The data reduction in CASA included WVR calibration; system temperature corrections; and bandpass, flux, and phase calibrations with Ceres and quasar J2258-2758.
Ceres and quasar J2258-2758 were used for absolute flux and bandpass calibration, respectively.
This 233 GHz continuum image was produced by CASA’s *CLEAN* algorithm using threshold of $\frac{1}{2}~ \sigma_{\rm RMS}$ and natural weighting.
using threshold of $\frac{1}{2}~ \sigma_{\rm RMS}$ and natural weighting

what.value: Model generation approach for debris ring (particles, thermal equilibrium grains)

evidence.quote: Models are generated using the same approach as in (cite: white) and assume a flat prior distribution.
We carry out the MCMC modelling in the image plane based on the method described in (cite: booth).
Following (cite: ricci), we adopt $\alpha_{pl} = 1.84 \pm 0.02$ and $\beta_{s} = 1.8 \pm 0.2$.

method.value: CASA CLEAN of 233 GHz continuum, natural weighting, threshold 0.5 sigma

evidence.quote: This 233 GHz continuum image was produced by CASA’s *CLEAN* algorithm using threshold of $\frac{1}{2}~ \sigma_{\rm RMS}$ and natural weighting.

analysis_steps.goal: Image-plane MCMC ring + point source fit

method.value: Model attenuated by primary beam, convolved with synthetic beam, compared to dirty image with chi^2; Metropolis-Hastings

evidence.quote: The model is attenuated by the primary beam and then convolved with the synthetic beam (the sampling function).

key_parameters.value: 3 chains, 100000 links, thinned by 10, sigma = 374 uJy

evidence.quote: The MCMC routine is run with 3 separate chains for a total of 100000 links (minus about 1000 each for burn-in).

assumptions.value: Gaussian radial profile, vertical Gaussian width 1 deg, point source at phase centre

evidence.quote: we assume that the vertical profile of the debris is Gaussian with a width of $1^\circ$
parameter space is explored using a random walk directed by a Metropolis-Hastings MCMC (cite: ford)

validation.value: ACF negligible for lags <=50; chains converge

evidence.quote: The ACF becomes negligible for lags of 50 or less for all thinned chains.

method.value: Predict model visibilities with setvp/predict and chi^2 on real and imaginary parts with weights

evidence.quote: used to “predict” the visibilities that the model would have for the actual array configuration and (u,v) coordinates using the tasks *setvp* and *predict*.
The MCMC routine is run with 10 separate chains for a total of 100000 links (minus about 1000 each for burn-in).
Uncertainties are given by a $95\%$ credible interval around the most probable value.

validation.value: Best model and data CLEANed, residuals inspected; compared with image-plane fit

evidence.quote: The data and best fit model are then deconvolved and imaged using the CASA CLEAN algorithm.

method.value: e from de-projected offsets over semi-major axis; mass from grain size distribution q=3.5

evidence.quote: the ring’s eccentricity can be calculated from the best fit semi-major axis and the X and Y offsets of the ellipse centre

assumptions.value: density 2.5 g/cc for 1.3 mm grains; 1 g/cc, Dmax 50 km for cascade

evidence.quote: Adopting an average density of 2.5$~g~cc^{-1}$, this approach yields a mass of M$_{\rm 1.3\,mm}\sim 0.017~M_{\bigoplus}$.

analysis_steps.goal: Spectral index and grain size slope

method.value: Bayesian MCMC fit of F_nu ∝ nu^alpha to ring fluxes; q=(alpha_mm-alpha_pl)/beta_s+3

evidence.quote: The posterior distribution for the spectral index is determined by performing a Bayesian parameter estimation for $F_\nu$.
Assuming a dust temperature of $45\pm5$ K yields $\alpha_{pl} = 1.84 \pm 0.02$
We use an MCMC approach similar to that used for the disc model fitting, incorporating the listed flux uncertainties, and assume a flat prior distribution.

validation.value: compared with Ricci et al. q and collisional cascade q=3.51

evidence.quote: Both of these results are also consistent with the predicted $q=3.51$

method.value: Bayesian black body fits to subsets of stellar flux data; 10% uncertainty when missing

evidence.quote: For data from literature, when the uncertainty is not given, a 10% uncertainty is used.

assumptions.value: Su et al. 870 um flux used rather than Boley

evidence.quote: The $870~\mu$m flux value from (cite: su16) was used in all further analysis.

fitting.value: Bayesian black body fit, 95% credible region

evidence.quote: The best fit brightness temperature and 95% credible region are given.

used_for.value: Calibration, CLEAN imaging, predict visibilities, exportfits

evidence.quote: Data were reduced using the Common Astronomy Software Applications (CASA) package (cite: casa_reference).
with a most probable flux of $0.90\pm 0.12$ mJy (including calibration uncertainties)

we find a total mass of M$(\rm D<50\,km) \sim 6~ M_{\bigoplus}$

findings_qualitative.value: No extended structure interior to the ring; central emission is a point source.

evidence.quote: no extended structure is found interior to the main ring

claims.hypothesis: Is there an inner debris component producing excess central emission?
claims.experiment: Fit ring + point source; compare central flux with photosphere extrapolation
claims.finding: No clear evidence for inner debris; stellar mm emission must be understood first

evidence.quote: the stellar flux is less than 70% of that predicted by extrapolating a black body

claims.hypothesis: Is the mm ring narrow and what is the grain size distribution?

evidence.quote: Both of these results are also consistent with the predicted $q=3.51$

claims.hypothesis: Does image-plane fitting match visibility fitting?
claims.finding: Visibility fitting necessary; image-plane for preliminary models

evidence.quote: We conclude that visibility fitting remains necessary, but image-plane fitting can be used to determine preliminary models.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Power law disc models were not well constrained

evidence.quote: Power law disc models were considered, but were not well constrained in the model fitting.

limitations_admitted.value: Ring ansae near primary beam edge, so N/S asymmetries and vertical structure unreliable

evidence.quote: As noted above, the ring ansae are close to the edges of the primary beam. As such, any potential North/South asymmetries are not reliable.

referee_caveats_inferred: Credible intervals for position angle table appear inverted
Stellar contribution at mm depends on assumed photosphere
